t: You're in the Abbey Garden, also known as the Canons' Garden, in Westminster. It's listed as an architectural structure designed by John Loughborough Pearson, a Gothic Revival architect famous for his churches and cathedrals. Pearson worked on at least two hundred and ten ecclesiastical buildings in England and was admired for reviving the craft of vaulting. There's little more on record about this particular spot, but it's a quiet reminder that his hand reached into the precincts of the Abbey.
